text.title: C# .NET Core Backend Failure Modes
text.summary: 13 antipatterns observed in real deployments. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Host process crashes silently mid-request; logs show `Unobserved task exception` with no stack frame in the codebase.
antipattern.root-cause: `async void` swallows the exception and tears down the process; the only legitimate use is a top-level event handler.
antipattern.fix: Change return type to `async Task`. Run a Roslyn analyzer (`VSTHRD100`) at CI to block reintroduction.

antipattern.symptom: Endpoint deadlocks under load; thread-pool starvation visible in `dotnet-counters`.
antipattern.root-cause: Author called `.Result` or `.Wait()` on an async API to avoid making the caller `async`.
antipattern.fix: Propagate `async` all the way up. Reviewers must reject any new `.Result`/`.Wait()`. Roslyn analyzer `VSTHRD002` enforces this.

antipattern.symptom: `BackgroundService` throws `InvalidOperationException: Cannot consume scoped service 'AppDbContext'` on first iteration — or worse, silently reuses one DbContext for the process lifetime.
antipattern.root-cause: Author injected `AppDbContext` into a singleton hosted service constructor.
antipattern.fix: Inject `IServiceScopeFactory` instead; create a scope per work unit inside `ExecuteAsync` (`using var scope = _scopeFactory.CreateScope();`).

antipattern.root-cause: Author forgot `await` on `ToListAsync()`/`FirstOrDefaultAsync()` and returned the Task.
antipattern.fix: Set `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` and enable `CS4014` to fail the build on un-awaited Tasks.

antipattern.symptom: Dev migration drops a column that prod still depends on; outage during next deploy.
antipattern.root-cause: Agent ran `dotnet ef database update` against a shared dev/prod DB without a human checkpoint.
antipattern.fix: Generate the SQL via `dotnet ef migrations script` for human review; gate destructive operations behind a confirmation prompt.

antipattern.symptom: Source-generated mapper (Mapperly) build error: `partial keyword required`.
antipattern.root-cause: Agent forgot the `partial` modifier on the mapper class declaration.
antipattern.fix: Add `partial` to the class declaration. Add a Roslyn analyzer or template snippet to enforce.

antipattern.symptom: Endpoint throws `AutoMapperMappingException: Missing type map` at first request after deploy.
antipattern.root-cause: `AddAutoMapper(...)` was called without the assembly that contains the `Profile`s.
antipattern.fix: Use `services.AddAutoMapper(typeof(Program).Assembly)` and assert `MapperConfiguration.AssertConfigurationIsValid()` in a unit test.

antipattern.symptom: `InvalidOperationException` on the second concurrent request, or two requests reading each other's tracked entities.
antipattern.root-cause: A service that holds `AppDbContext` was registered with `AddSingleton<IUserService, UserService>()`, capturing a Scoped dependency for the process lifetime. `DbContext` is not thread-safe.
antipattern.fix: Register every DbContext-touching service as `AddScoped<,>()`. Turn on DI scope validation in all environments (`ValidateScopes = true`) so the container fails at startup instead of at first load.

antipattern.symptom: Test project fails to compile: "Cannot find type Program" from `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`.
antipattern.root-cause: `public partial class Program { }` was left off the bottom of `Program.cs`, so the entry point type is not visible to the test assembly.
antipattern.fix: Add the partial declaration to `Program.cs` and keep it in the scaffolding template so it cannot be dropped again.

antipattern.symptom: A controller or service injects `IServiceProvider` and calls `GetService<T>()` inside methods; unit tests cannot substitute the dependency and a missing registration surfaces only at first request.
antipattern.root-cause: Service locator hides dependencies from the constructor signature, so the container's startup validation never sees them.
antipattern.fix: Move every dependency to constructor injection. The only permitted `IServiceProvider`/`IServiceScopeFactory` use is scope creation inside a `BackgroundService`.

antipattern.symptom: Connection string or API key visible in `appsettings.json` in the repository.
antipattern.root-cause: appsettings is the path of least resistance, and the agent has no signal that the file is committed.
antipattern.fix: Move the value to `dotnet user-secrets` locally and to environment variables or a managed secret store in production; add a pre-commit grep for connection strings and rotate whatever was committed.

antipattern.symptom: `[AllowAnonymous]` appears on a controller, or a CORS policy allows `*` with credentials, in a diff whose stated purpose was fixing a local 401.
antipattern.root-cause: Development friction is resolved with the smallest config change that makes the error go away; the change ships to production unchanged.
antipattern.fix: Revert the attribute; fix the local auth setup instead. Treat every new `[AllowAnonymous]`, role policy and CORS entry as a named human checkpoint in review.

antipattern.symptom: Throughput drops under load while CPU stays low; `dotnet-counters` shows thread-pool queue growth.
antipattern.root-cause: `Task.Run` inside a handler was used to "make it async"; it takes a thread from the same pool that serves requests and the work dies on shutdown.
antipattern.fix: Delete the `Task.Run`. If the work is genuinely background, hand it to a hosted service through a bounded `Channel<T>`.
